section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the story of Rebbi placing Rabbi Chiya and his sons before the ark, and the question of why their prayer only caused wind, rain, and an earthquake when they served as the public's emissaries.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter in more detail,
will be understood according to what is brought in the Gemara,
that when Rebbi heard from Eliyahu the prophet that Rabbi Chiya and his sons are comparable to the Patriarchs,
Rebbi stood them before the ark,
he said "Who makes the wind blow" and a wind blew,
"Who brings down the rain" and rain came,
when he reached saying "Who revives the dead" the world trembled.
And the Alshich wrote
that the request "Ad-noy, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise" which is at the beginning of the silent prayer,
is that our prayer should be like the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons.
And it is not understood,
how can it be said that our prayer should be like the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons
[and especially according to what is brought in the Gemara there that Rabbi Chiya and his sons were like the Patriarchs].
Also, it needs to be understood,
that Rabbi Chiya and his sons would pray every day,
and nevertheless the drawing down through the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons
(a wind blew,
rain came,
the world trembled)
was specifically when Rebbi stood them before the ark.
For through their praying before the ark and being the emissaries of the congregation,
their prayer had the power of the congregation,
for regarding the prayer of many
(the prayer of the congregation)
it is written,
"Behold, the Almighty is great and does not despise."
And although the prayer of the congregation exists every day,
and that it was specifically through this prayer that a wind blew etc. is because of the virtue of Rabbi Chiya and his sons who were comparable to the Patriarchs,
nevertheless,
even regarding the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons, in order for there to be a wind blowing etc., it was specifically when they were the emissaries of the congregation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the difference between individual and congregational prayer is that congregational prayer draws influence down into physicality, and that Rabbi Chiya and his sons' personal prayer drew only spiritually until they became the public's emissaries.
section.t: And ostensibly, it could be explained this way according to what is known,
that from the fact that in every request in the silent prayer we conclude "Blessed are You, Ad-noy",
it is proven,
that even in an individual's prayer there is absolutely no doubt that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills his request.
Rather, in an individual's prayer it is possible that the influence will be drawn down for him above,
or that it will be drawn down
(also below,
but only)
in spirituality,
and the advantage of congregational prayer
(which is desirable and accepted forever)
is,
that the influence is drawn down also below in physicality.
And behold, in congregational prayer,
there are several levels of gradations,
and the greater the request is,
and especially when the congregation praying are not fitting vessels for it,
a greater prayer is needed,
and also that the emissary of the congregation should be an elder
(or the most distinguished of the congregation)
so that his prayer will be heard.
And based on this, it could ostensibly be explained regarding Rabbi Chiya and his sons,
that this—that through their prayer when they were emissaries of the congregation a wind blew and rain came
(in physicality)
is
(primarily)
due to the advantage of the prayer of many,
except that even in congregational prayer
(and especially for a great request that the congregation is not worthy of it),
it is necessary that the emissary of the congregation be one whose prayer is heard.
But this explanation is insufficient,
for from that which they said that Rabbi Chiya and his sons were comparable to the Patriarchs,
it implies,
that this—that through their prayer a wind blew and rain came—is because of the greatness of their elevation
(that their prayer is heard like the prayer of the Patriarchs),
and nevertheless,
this—that a wind blew etc.—was specifically when they were emissaries of the congregation.
And the matter is,
that this—that the drawing down through prayer is in physicality
[to the extent that through the drawing down a change is made in the creations,
to heal the sick and bless the years,
and unlike the drawing down through Torah and mitzvos which is
(primarily)
above]
is when the drawing down in physicality is from the requests of the needs of the one praying
[except that even then there are several levels of gradations.
For in addition to the difference between an individual's prayer and the prayer of many,
there is also a difference in the level of the person praying
(the individual,
or the emissary of the congregation),
for there is one whose prayer is heard more].
And since the drawings down of "Who makes the wind blow" etc. were not from the requests of the needs of Rabbi Chiya and his sons,
therefore,
through their prayer
(when they prayed by themselves)
they drew down these matters in spirituality
(similar to the drawing down through Torah and mitzvos),
and when Rebbi stood them before the ark and they became emissaries of the congregation of all of Israel,
through this these matters were included in the requests of their needs
[in addition to that through their praying as emissaries of the congregation of all of Israel, the advantage of the power of the many was added to their prayer],
and therefore,
through their prayer then, the matters were drawn down also in physicality.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the drawing down into the physical world required the element of Torah, which Rebbi added by standing them before the ark, while the power to effect change came from their superior prayer of self-nullification like the Patriarchs.
section.t: And there is another matter in this,
that this—that through the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons
[even when they were emissaries of the congregation and the matters of "Who makes the wind blow" etc. became requests of their needs]
a wind blew etc.—is because Rebbi, who was the prince of Torah,
stood them before the ark,
and through this, their prayer also contained the aspect of Torah.
And the matter is,
that in the drawing down through prayer, which is the service of the lower one,
the state of the lower one matters,
and in order for influence to be drawn down to the lower one, it is specifically when he is
(somewhat)
a vessel for the drawing down.
And the drawing down through Torah,
since it is from above,
is drawn down to the lowest level,
even when the lower one is not a vessel
(at all)
for the drawing down.
Therefore,
this—that through the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons the drawing down was in the world
(even though the world was then not a vessel for this)
is through that in their prayer there was
(also)
the aspect of Torah
(through Rebbi standing them before the ark).
And that the drawing down was specifically through the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons
(and not through Rebbi),
is,
for in order for there to be a change in the physical, it is through the drawing down of the Ein Sof light that is above the chain of descent,
for the drawing down of this light is specifically through the elevation of feminine waters of prayer.
And in this matter,
Rabbi Chiya and his sons were greater than Rebbi.
For the advantage of prayer,
which is the elevation of feminine waters to draw down the Ein Sof light that is above the chain of descent,
is the self-nullification in prayer,
that the person praying is like a servant before his master,
and Rabbi Chiya and his sons were comparable to the Patriarchs,
who were a chariot for G-dliness,
for a chariot is utter self-nullification.
And therefore,
the prayer of Rabbi Chiya and his sons was an elevation of feminine waters to draw down a most exalted light,
through which drawing down a change is made in the creations,
even to the change of the revival of the dead.
Except that in order for the drawing down to be in the world
(even though the world is not a vessel for this)
it is through that in their prayer there was
(also)
the aspect of Torah,
a drawing down from above.
